intro: Anesthesiologists have rare clinical skills, so no career outside medicine is a close match. The best fits among the 25 careers below reach only a 50% skill match, led by Athletic Trainers, and all pay far less than the $391,490 median anesthesiologists earn, according to BLS May 2025 data.
why_it_works: Your work combines fast judgment, deep knowledge of drugs and physiology, and calm control in the operating room. O*NET rates judgment and decision making at 4.25 out of 5 for this job. Few occupations ask for that mix, which is why the matches below are weak. Many physicians who step back move into teaching, research or administration that this list cannot fully capture.
tips: Consider part-time or locum work before leaving medicine; it keeps your license and income while you explore.
Medical Dosimetrists are the best-paid match at $147,470 and use your knowledge of dosing and safety.
Teaching roles in medical schools are not separate careers in this data; ask your hospital about academic positions.

faq.q: What jobs can former anesthesiologists do?
faq.a: The closest matches by skills are Athletic Trainers (50%), Orthotists and Prosthetists (47%) and postsecondary chemistry teachers (46%), based on O*NET 31.0. These are weak matches. Many anesthesiologists who leave practice stay in medicine through teaching, consulting or hospital leadership instead.

faq.q: Which careers for anesthesiologists pay the most?
faq.a: None of the 25 matches pay more than the $391,490 median. The highest are Medical Dosimetrists at $147,470 (62% less), health and safety engineers at $115,160 (71% less) and postsecondary engineering teachers at $109,270 (72% less), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do anesthesiologists need more education to change careers?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than anesthesiologists already have. In the closest matches, a master's degree is the most common level, held by 54% of workers, so your medical degree more than covers the formal requirements of any job on this list.

faq.q: What skills would anesthesiologists need for a new career?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment selection, programming, instructing and coordination. Complex problem solving and social perceptiveness already rate 4 out of 5 for anesthesiologists in O*NET, so teaching and technical roles are the most realistic directions for most people.
